issues.legal_issue: Compensation for acquired market land must reflect relevant comparable sales and evidence of the land’s location, development, and rising prices.
material_facts: The acquired property was market land that had been leased out.
Two nearby sales of leasehold rights were considered relevant; the High Court had averaged their prices when fixing compensation.
Witnesses described increasing land prices, nearby shops and houses, new roads, and growth in the locality.
The Supreme Court found the acquired land similar to land in connected appeals for which it upheld a higher compensation rate.
issues.conclusion: The claimant’s appeal was allowed and compensation was fixed at Rs. 15,000 per Bigha, with an additional 15% for compulsory acquisition and 6% annual interest on the additional amount from possession until payment. The Collector’s appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Market value is assessed from relevant comparable transactions together with evidence bearing on the land’s location, development, and price trends; the nature of the interests sold is relevant when comparing sale prices. The Court also relied on its valuation of similar land in connected appeals. The acquisition was notified under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894; the judgment does not cite a separate valuation provision or an earlier reported case.

rule.if: acquisition_compensation_appeal and market_land and comparable_leasehold_sales and locality_developing_and_prices_rising and similar_to_land_with_higher_approved_valuation

predicates.acquisition_compensation_appeal: A party appealed the compensation fixed for land acquired for a public purpose.
predicates.market_land: The acquired land was used as market land and was being leased out.
predicates.comparable_leasehold_sales: Evidence included nearby sales of leasehold interests considered relevant to valuing the acquired land.
predicates.locality_developing_and_prices_rising: Evidence showed that the locality was developing and that land prices there were increasing.
predicates.similar_to_land_with_higher_approved_val: The court found the acquired land similar to other acquired land for which it had upheld a higher valuation.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal concerns market land and relevant comparable sales, rising prices in a developing locality, and similarity to land with a higher approved valuation are established, compensation is enhanced to reflect market value.
